review_comments.body:
**Invalid string IDs now raise ValueError subclasses, not TypeError** · correctness This applies when `delete`, `forget`, `activity_log`, `get_import` or the group methods get a non-numeric or empty string such as `"abcdefgh"` or `""`. `path_id` raises `InvalidIdError` or `EmptyIdError`, and both subclass `ValueError`, so the old `TypeError` no longer comes out. The existing test `tests/subscribers_test.py::test_given_invalid_subscriber_id_when_calling_delete_...` runs `pytest.raises(TypeError)` on `delete("abcdefgh")` and will now fail. Callers that catch `TypeError` also stop catching these errors. Every docstring still says `:raises: TypeError`. Meanwhile `get` and `update` still raise `TypeError` for the same inputs, so the class is inconsistent. The new tests hide this: the ID-only test accepts any of the three exception types. **Suggested fix** Pick one behaviour. Either keep `TypeError` for these methods, for example by wrapping `path_id` and re-raising `ValueError` as `TypeError`, or deliberately switch to the new exceptions. In the second case, update the existing test in `tests/subscribers_test.py` and the `:raises:` docstrings, and make `get` and `update` consistent.
Prompt for a coding agent ``` In mailerlite/sdk/subscribers.py, the methods delete, forget, activity_log, get_import, assign_subscriber_to_group and unassign_subscriber_from_group now call path_id, which raises EmptyIdError/InvalidIdError (ValueError subclasses) for bad strings. The existing test tests/subscribers_test.py::test_given_invalid_subscriber_id_when_calling_delete_then_returning_subscirber_will_fail expects TypeError and will fail. Either keep TypeError for these methods, or update that test and the `:raises:` docstrings to document EmptyIdError/InvalidIdError. Keep get/update consistent with whatever is chosen. ```

## Confidence Score: 3/5 **[Medium risk]** The reported P1 stands: the ID-only methods now raise ValueError subclasses (InvalidIdError, EmptyIdError) instead of TypeError for invalid strings like "abcdefgh" or "", which breaks the existing tests/subscribers_test.py expectation and callers catching TypeError, while get and update still raise TypeError. The risk is medium because the change is ordinary application logic that a revert undoes cleanly, with no data, security or infrastructure effect. ## Findings - [`mailerlite/sdk/subscribers.py:184`](https://github.com/mailerlite/mailerlite-python/blob/20a43437360bbab23836187f9ce60fb3e769f6a2/mailerlite/sdk/subscribers.py#L184) [Invalid string IDs now raise ValueError subclasses, not TypeError](https://github.com/mailerlite/mailerlite-python/pull/111#discussion_r4527203341) · correctness ### Summary Accepts numeric string IDs across subscriber methods Subscriber ID-only methods now use the shared `path_id` validator, and `get`/`update` accept digit-only strings through `_is_id`. IDs go into the URL path unchanged. Invalid IDs in the ID-only methods now raise `InvalidIdError` or `EmptyIdError` (both `ValueError`) instead of `TypeError`. **What's good** - The new tests assert on the exact request path and verb, and check that no request is sent for invalid IDs. - The digit check uses `fullmatch` on an ASCII pattern, so trailing newlines and non-ASCII digits are rejected.
